code.text: Acute on chronic left fronto-parietal subdural haematoma, status post burr hole drainage, in subacute recovery
Falls risk with persistent unsteadiness and functional decline post-subdural haematoma

resource.valueString: Intermittent dull left-sided headache, 2–3/10, worse when overtired; stable low-intensity pattern. No sudden severe or different headache, early-morning vomiting, or nocturnal headache waking him.

Patient and daughter report he is somewhat more forgetful; misplaces items and repeats questions. Patient feels he has always been absent-minded. Sometimes delayed recalling exact dates; able to recount hospital stay and daily routine with an overall consistent account. No getting lost in familiar places; continues basic routines. Formal cognitive screening has not yet been performed.

Feels somewhat wobbly, especially on first standing or in dim light; unsteady on quick turns and reports using furniture for support indoors. One near-fall while turning quickly in the kitchen in the past 2 weeks; caught himself on a bench. No further actual falls since discharge. Gait could not be observed during phone consultation.

code.text: Activities of daily living and function

resource.valueString: Independent with basic self-care but slower; sits for showers because of fear of falling. Manages simple meals. No longer does ladder, roof, or garden work. Not driving as advised by hospital. Relies on daughter for shopping and transport to appointments; daughter has arranged direct debit for bills, and patient is not managing complex finances himself.
Broken sleep; wakes 2–3 times overnight thinking. No nocturnal headache waking him.
Denies low mood; acknowledges frustration about decreased independence. Denies suicidal ideation.
Occasional fuzzy vision when tired. Denies diplopia and acute visual loss.
Denies dysarthria, dysphasia, and swallowing issues. Speech fluent during phone consultation, with no word-finding difficulty reported over the phone.
No seizure history before or after the subdural haematoma.

Denies new focal weakness, numbness, facial asymmetry, new incontinence, acute visual loss, or rapid increase in confusion. No current history features of acute rebleed or raised intracranial pressure were reported; phone assessment was limited.

Described himself as mostly alright. Alert, conversant, and oriented in conversation to person, place, and time. Speaking in full sentences with no audible shortness of breath. Engaged, polite, and coherent; tended to minimise symptoms.

Hospital discharge summary reports CT brain approximately 6 weeks ago, after burr hole evacuation of left fronto-parietal chronic subdural haematoma: small residual collection, minimal midline shift, no acute haemorrhage, and no hydrocephalus. No repeat imaging since.
Wonders whether an old mattress and water tasting different might be contributing to symptoms; clinician reassured him these were unlikely to be secondary to the subdural haematoma.

Lives alone in a one-bedroom public housing flat; retired electrician on an age pension with limited finances. Daughter is main support, approximately 30 minutes away, checks weekly, and assists with shopping, transport, and bills. No formal home care package or My Aged Care services in place. Patient is anxious about possible move or rent change and housing stability.

dosage.text: 1 g up to three times daily as needed; self-limits to approximately 2 g/day most days

note.text: Patient reports regular use as needed, self-limiting to approximately 2 g/day most days. Advised maximum 4 g in 24 hours.
